input.question: Why would someone go onto a TV "judge" show when they're blatantly in the wrong?
input.ground_truth: Both parties have a pool of money that they are paid in order to appear on the show. If any money is owed to the plaintiff or defender, it is subtracted from that pool, and then the pool is evenly divided between the two parties that have agreed to show up. Question: Why would someone go onto a TV "judge" show when they're blatantly in the wrong?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friend are playing a game, but you took your friend’s toy without asking. If a grown-up (like a TV judge) asks you both to come and talk about what happened, you might still want to go—even if you know you did something not so nice.

Why? Maybe you hope the grown-up will be nice to you, or maybe you want to explain your side. Or maybe you just want to see what happens on TV. Sometimes people go on those shows even when they know they did something wrong because they want to tell their story, or they hope the judge will be understanding, or maybe they just want to be on TV and get attention. But it’s not always the smartest thing to do!
